summary: Validated release-build regression scope for AiForge: Expo web preview loads on mobile viewport, eas.json build types are correct, Expo prebuild config resolves with expected Android package/plugins, Android JS export with --no-bytecode succeeds (3950 modules), and backend health endpoints are reachable. One backend integration failure remains on /api/editor/caption (502) due to upstream Azure 401.

critical.issue: Returns 502 via public ingress after successful auth. Backend logs show repeated Azure chat/completions 401 PermissionDenied, which propagates to caption failure.

minor.issue: Returns 404 (health is exposed at /health internal and /api/ root for ingress checks).

action_items: Fix Azure text credentials/deployment for caption flow (backend log: chat/completions 401 PermissionDenied) or add resilient fallback provider for /api/editor/caption.
If external monitors expect /api/health, add an alias route to reduce ambiguity; current valid health checks are /health (internal) and /api/ (ingress).
critical_code_review_comments: frontend/app/editor.tsx is >1000 lines; split into focused modules/hooks to reduce regression risk.
frontend/app/creation/[id].tsx decodeBase64 fallback uses Buffer without explicit import/polyfill guard; this can fail on some native runtimes if Buffer is unavailable.
Many interactive elements in editor.tsx subcomponents still lack explicit testID, limiting robust mobile UI automation coverage.
seed_data_creation: No new persistent seed data added. Existing test suites used demo auth and transient requests only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Release config checks are green. Re-run caption and related text-generation endpoints after Azure key/deployment correction, then rerun test_playstore_readiness.py and mobile preview smoke.
rca_of_issue: Reproduction: login via /api/auth/login (demo@example.com), then call /api/editor/caption with bearer token. Result: 502. Backend err log shows HTTP Request to Azure chat/completions -> 401 PermissionDenied, causing caption generation failure upstream.
